label: prf:s4-s3-half-symmetric-projection
title: Proof of s4 s3 half symmetric projection
html:
Proof. By the standard S_n branching rule (remove one box from the Young diagram of \lambda \vdash 4 to obtain the restriction \lambda \downarrow S_3):

\lambda \vdash 4 \dim V_\lambda \lambda \downarrow S_3 Trivial (3) content
(4) 1 (3) 1
(3,1) 3 (3) + (2,1) 1
(2,2) 2 (2,1) 0
(2,1,1) 3 (2,1) + (1^3) 0
(1^4) 1 (1^3) 0

The half-symmetric H_4 projection includes one representative of each conjugate pair \{(4), (1^4)\} and \{(3,1), (2,1,1)\}, plus \tfrac{1}{2} of the self-conjugate (2,2):

  \dim_{\text{half-sym}} = 1 + 3 + 1 = 5, \qquad
  \text{trivial } S_3 \text{ content} = 1 + 1 + 0 = 2.

The S_3-trivial projection factor is

  \frac{\text{trivial content}}{\text{total half-sym dim}}
  = \frac{2}{5}.

Applied to the 8-fold ideal-octahedral tessellation of S^3 \setminus \mathcal{B}_3 (Adams 1985 [adams1985hyperbolic]: \mathrm{Vol}(\mathcal{B}_3) = 8G where G = \Lambda(\pi/4) = \tfrac{1}{2} V_{\text{oct}} is Catalan's constant):

  \text{effective cell count}
  = \underbrace{\tfrac{5}{2}}_{\text{half-sym count}}
    \times \underbrace{\tfrac{2}{5}}_{S_3\text{-trivial factor}}
  = 1.

The per-cell ratio is 1/8, confirming that the half-symmetric projection selects exactly one of the eight ideal octahedral cells. The reading is purely structural — which cell is identified, not how much per-cell curvature it carries. \square
